subject: Per-token corridor offsets & clawback structure for Grok Labs
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: James Thompson <james@groklabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial corridor + clawback sketch for Grok Labs (per-token)

James —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, sketching a few concrete constructs so we can get alignment on which pricing lens you want us to model (marginal vs blended) and where to put the true-up/clawback guardrails. High-level ask: which of these feels closest to your procurement comfort level so we can turn this into a legal-ready term sheet.

Option A — Marginal ladder (simple, most transparent)
- Breakpoints (monthly committed tokens): 0-150M @ $0.00062 / token; 150-450M @ $0.00049; 450M+ @ $0.00037
- You pay the marginal price for tokens in each band (standard marginal math).
- True-up monthly with quarterly reconciliation. No clawback unless actuals are >40% below committed corridor across a quarter.

Option B — Blended effective rate (predictable invoice)
- Commit 300M tokens monthly, blended rate example: $0.00052 / token (weighted average across expected consumption bands).
- True-up quarterly with an effective-rate true-up invoice. Clawback mechanics only if you exit the agreement early.

Option C — Corridor + smoothing (hybrid, reduces cliff risk) — what I think Grok prefers
- Commit corridor: lower bound 250M / month, upper bound 400M / month.
- Floor protection: if consumption falls below 80% of lower bound across a quarter, credits apply rather than cash clawback (limited to 6 months of credits).
- Overuse above corridor billed at next marginal band price, with automatic content-preserving fallbacks (we can route lower-cost variants to reduce spend spikes).
- Clawback: only for systematic underutilization (>50% below lower bound for two consecutive quarters) with pro-rated credit recapture.

Notes: these numbers are starter points. For clarity, I included a small modeling workbook (Grok_Usage_Forecast.xlsx) with three scenarios (base / upsell / slowdown) so finance can see blended vs marginal P&L.

Next steps: tell us which option to model, and Ben will run a 12-month invoice walk showing both marginal and blended outcomes. If you want, we can also show a smoothing variant that phases prices over 6 months to blunt cliff effects.

Thanks,
Rafael
Sales, Redwood Inference
Rafael Mendes | rafael@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Grok_Usage_Forecast.xlsx (xlsx, forecast workbook)
From: James Thompson <james@groklabs.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial corridor + clawback sketch for Grok Labs (per-token)

Rafael —

Appreciate the detailed options. A few immediate clarifying questions before we pick:
1) On Option A (marginal) — how would you handle a month where we spike to 600M tokens because of a product launch? Will we be invoiced at marginal rates that month and then true-up? Any burst credits?
2) On Option B (blended) — can you produce an example invoice vs actual meter so we can see cashflow impact in a downside case (we under-consume by 40% for q1)?
3) Option C sounds attractive; curious what you mean by "content-preserving fallbacks" — can you guarantee model family substitution won't materially change output accuracy? We need a signal path if a fallback happens.

Also cc'ing our contracts mailbox — they want to be kept looped in early.

—James
James Thompson
Head of Platform Ops, Grok Labs
James.Thompson@groklabs.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: James Thompson <james@groklabs.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial corridor + clawback sketch for Grok Labs (per-token)

James — quick math attached and a short note on the margin vs blended tradeoffs.

If you spike to 600M in a month under Option A (marginal):
- You pay marginal band pricing for tokens in each band that month. Example invoice for 600M: first 150M @ $0.00062 = $93,000; next 300M @ $0.00049 = $147,000; final 150M @ $0.00037 = $55,500; total = $295,500; effective blended = $0.0004925/token.

Under a blended 300M commit at $0.00052 with actual 180M consumed (down 40%):
- You still owe the committed charge on invoice (300M * $0.00052 = $156,000) unless we agree to a crediting/true-up mechanism. Typically we do quarterly true-up: if you under-consume, the shortfall converts to credits applied against future invoices for up to 6 months.

On the content-preservation question for Option C: our fallback is to model-family equivalents validated by our QA team. That means we guarantee baseline semantic/intent parity across the two selected variants for your primary prompt families. We will provide a fallback policy and a webhook to notify you when a fallback is used and which model variant served the request. We can include a 30-day SLA credit if fallbacks exceed X% of total tokens in a month (threshold to be agreed).

Attached: Redwood_Modeling_Matrix.xlsx (simple invoice scenarios) and a draft fallback policy paragraph for inclusion in the SLA.

Let me know which scenario you want run across your three forecast cases; Rafael, do you want me to prepare a 12-month blended vs marginal comparison for the legal term sheet?

Cheers,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: James Thompson <james@groklabs.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Grok Labs Contracts <contracts@groklabs.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 13:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial corridor + clawback sketch for Grok Labs (per-token)

Thanks Ben — that helps a lot. Two follow-ups from our side:
- Can you add a smoothing ramp so our effective rate moves from $0.00060 down to the target tier over 6 months if we commit to a two-year deal? That eases our CFO’s concern about step-changes.
- For the crediting on under-consumption, we want a clause that credits unused committed tokens at a 70% recovery rate (i.e., for each unconsumed token you credit us 0.7 * the committed price) and that credits can roll forward for up to 9 months. Is that something Redwood can accept?

Contracts: we will want a short clawback window, but prefer credits first. If legal needs numbers to model, let us know.

—James
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: James Thompson <james@groklabs.com>, Grok Labs Contracts <contracts@groklabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 15:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial corridor + clawback sketch for Grok Labs (per-token)

James —

Thanks — good, actionable asks. Agreed next actions and responses inline below:
1) Smoothing ramp: yes, we can present a 6-month phased discount schedule tied to a 24-month commit. Example: months 1–2: 75% of target tier discount; months 3–4: 90%; months 5–6: 100% (target). We will model the invoice cashflow impact for CFO.
2) Credit recovery rate: 70% recovery on unused committed tokens with 9-month roll-forward is reasonable from a commercial perspective; I will flag final legal carve-outs (e.g., abnormal events clause).
3) Burst protection: we propose a burst pool (one-time annual burst credits equal to 20% of monthly upper bound) to cover launches. Excess is billed at overage marginal rates.
4) SLA/fallback: we will include the webhook notification and a monthly fallback volume report; threshold SLA credits to be proposed in the draft SLA.

Attached: Redwood_Draft_SLA.pdf (contains fallback paragraph + SLA credit table) and I updated Grok_Usage_Forecast.xlsx with the smoothing scenario. Ben will prepare the 12-month marginal vs blended invoice comparison by EOD Monday for your contracts team.

If that all sounds OK, Ben and I will convert into a narrow term sheet for Contracts to redline.

Best,
Rafael
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
